twinSimulator.pageSubtitle: Enter a few monthly numbers and compare three possible versions of your financial future: what happens if nothing changes, what improves if you adjust your habits, and what could go wrong if spending or surprise costs rise.
twinSimulator.introBody: This is a planning sandbox, not a forecast. It helps you see which daily choices have the biggest effect on savings, debt, and your goal.
twinSimulator.formHelper: Use approximate monthly numbers. The simulator is most useful when the inputs feel realistic, even if they are not perfect.
twinSimulator.summaryHelper: Each card shows where you could land by the end of your timeline. Money after debt means savings and investments minus unpaid debt.
twinSimulator.chartTitle: Money After Debt, Month by Month
twinSimulator.chartHelper: The line chart tracks savings minus debt over time. A higher line means more room to fund goals or handle emergencies.
twinSimulator.disclaimerBody: This tool is for learning and planning only. It does not recommend financial products, promise investment returns, or replace advice from a qualified professional.
twinSimulator.noResultText: Run the simulation to see how your current habits, better habits, and a riskier path compare.

current.title: Current habits
current.body: Keeps your income, spending, debt payment, and savings exactly as entered.

improved.title: Better habits
improved.body: Cuts lifestyle spending by 20% and food/transport by 10%. If you still have debt, 60% of the extra cash goes to debt and 40% goes to savings.

risky.title: Riskier path
risky.body: Raises flexible spending and adds one surprise cost during the timeline, so you can see how fragile the plan might be.

fields.riskBehavior: Risk setting for the riskier path

fieldHelp.monthlyIncome: Use the amount that actually reaches your account each month.
fieldHelp.currentSavings: Include cash, savings, and investments you could use toward this goal.
fieldHelp.essentialSpending: Rent, bills, school fees, insurance, and other costs you cannot easily skip.
fieldHelp.lifestyleSpending: Eating out, entertainment, hobbies, shopping, subscriptions, and treats.
fieldHelp.foodTransportSpending: Regular meals, groceries, commuting, ride-hailing, fuel, and parking.
fieldHelp.otherSpending: Anything monthly that does not fit the categories above.
fieldHelp.debtBalance: The unpaid amount across loans, credit cards, installments, or paylater.
fieldHelp.monthlyDebtPayment: The amount you normally pay toward debt every month.
fieldHelp.goalAmount: The amount you want to have saved by the end of the timeline.
fieldHelp.timeHorizon: How many months you want the simulator to look ahead.
fieldHelp.expectedReturn: A simple yearly growth assumption for savings or investments. Use 0 if you do not want to assume growth.
fieldHelp.riskBehavior: This controls how much extra spending and how large the surprise cost is in the riskier path.

biggestBottleneck.overspending: The biggest drag is flexible spending. Too much of your monthly income is leaving before it can become savings or debt reduction.
biggestBottleneck.highDebt: Debt is the biggest drag. A large part of your cash flow is tied up in repayments instead of moving toward your goal.
biggestBottleneck.shortHorizon: The goal may be too large for the timeline. The plan improves, but it may need more months to work.
biggestBottleneck.lowIncome: Your income is stretched compared with the goal and monthly expenses. Spending control helps, but income may also need attention.
biggestBottleneck.alreadyAtGoal: You already have enough saved for this target. The next step is protecting it and deciding what to do with any extra cash flow.
biggestBottleneck.noSavingsCapacity: There is almost no monthly room left after spending and debt payments. The plan needs breathing space before it can grow.

bestNextAction.cutLifestyleSpending: Start with one or two flexible spending cuts and send that money directly to savings or debt. Small recurring changes matter most here.
bestNextAction.buildEmergencyFund: Build an emergency buffer first, so one surprise expense does not push the plan backward.
bestNextAction.focusOnDebt: Prioritize the most expensive debt and keep repayments consistent. Reducing debt improves every future month.
bestNextAction.extendHorizon: Give the goal more time or split it into smaller milestones. That makes the monthly pressure more realistic.
bestNextAction.increaseIncome: Look for additional income while keeping expenses steady. Extra income has the biggest effect when it is not absorbed by new spending.
bestNextAction.maintainGoodHabits: You are already in a strong position. Keep the habit, protect the money, and review the plan regularly.

first.name: Danny Sudarsono
first.testimony: As a corporate professional who is also building a startup, I feel that Docduit can provide financial advice comparable to top-tier wealth management services. It's quite cool to get AI-based advice from Docduit.

second.name: Hasna Luthfiana
second.testimony: As a new jobber, I feel very helped by the Docduit website! Consulting with AI makes me feel more comfortable talking about my financial conditions. I often felt confused about who to ask when faced with financial problems. But with Docduit, I can get new insights and relevant advice without feeling awkward. As I'm still learning to manage finances at the start of my career, Docduit is truly the right solution.

third.name: Azka Adziman
third.occupation: Undergraduate Student at Oxford University | Clash of Champions Season 3
third.testimony: As a university student, Docduit's financial calculators are certainly very useful. They not only break down the targets you need to achieve each month, but also recommend investment tools that can help you achieve your dreams faster, such as foreign currency and gold. If you want to buy a new gadget or save for a vacation, you should try Docduit!
